paragraphs.sourceText: The economy grew, trade increased, and millions of new jobs were created. How can biological indicators show the 28 of economic indicators?

The answer is that the economic indicators have a basic fault; they show no difference between resource uses that 29 progress and those uses that will hurt it. The main measure of economic progress is the gross national product (GNP). 30 , this totals the value of all goods and services produced and subtracts loss in value of factories and equipment. Developed a half-century ago, GNP helped 31 a common way among countries of measuring change in economic output. For some time, this seemed to work 32 well, but serious weaknesses are now appearing. As indicated earlier, GNP includes loss in value of factories and equipment, but it does not 33 the loss of natural resources, including nonrenewable resources such as oil or renewable resources such as forests.

This basic fault can produce a 34 sense of national economic health. According to GNP, for example, countries that overcut forests actually do better than those that preserve their forests. The trees cut down are counted as income but no subtraction is made for 35 the forests.

paragraphs.sourceText: Directions：In this section, you are going to read a passage with ten statements attached to it. Each statement contains information given in one of the paragraphs. Identify the paragraph from which the information is derived. You may choose a paragraph more than once. Each paragraph is marked with a letter. Answer the questions by marking the corresponding letter on Answer Sheet 2. The Changes Facing Fast Food
paragraphs.translationZh: 说明：在本节中，您将阅读一段附有十个陈述的段落。每条陈述都包含其中一个段落中给出的信息。确定信息来源的段落。您可以多次选择一个段落。每个段落都标有一个字母。在答题卡上标记相应的字母来回答问题 2. 快餐面临的变化

paragraphs.sourceText: A) Fast-food firms have to be a thick-skinned bunch. Health experts regularly criticise them severely for selling food that makes people fat. Critics even complain that McDonald’s, whose logo symbolises calorie excess, should not have been allowed to sponsor the World Cup. These are things fast-food firms have learnt to cope with. But not perhaps for much longer. The burger business faces more pressure from regulators at a time when it is already adapting strategies in response to shifts in the global economy.
paragraphs.translationZh: A）快餐公司必须是一群脸皮厚的人。健康专家经常严厉批评他们出售使人发胖的食品。批评者甚至抱怨麦当劳的标志象征着卡路里过量，不应该被允许赞助世界杯。快餐公司已经学会应对这些问题。但也许不会持续太久。当汉堡行业已经在调整策略以应对全球经济变化时，它面临着来自监管机构的更大压力。

paragraphs.sourceText: B) Fast food was once thought to be recession-proof. When consumers need to cut spending, the logic goes，cheap meals like Big Macs and Whoppers become even more attractive. Such “trading down” proved true for much of the latest recession, when fast-food companies picked up customers who could no longer afford to eat at casual restaurants. Traffic was boosted in America, the home of fast food, with discounts and promotions, such as $ 1 menus and cheap combination meals.
paragraphs.translationZh: B) 快餐一度被认为可以抵御经济衰退。按照逻辑，当消费者需要削减开支时，巨无霸和皇堡等廉价食品就变得更具吸引力。在最近的经济衰退的大部分时间里，这种“降级消费”被证明是正确的，当时快餐公司吸引了那些再也无力在休闲餐厅吃饭的顾客。快餐之乡美国的客流量因 1 美元菜单和廉价组合餐等折扣和促销活动而增加。

paragraphs.sourceText: C) As a result, fast-food chains have weathered the recession better than their more expensive competitors. In 2009 sales at full-service restaurants in America fell by more than 6% , but total sales remained about the same at fast-food chains. In some markets, such as Japan, France and Britain, total spending on fast food increased. Same-store sales in America at McDonald’s, the world’s largest fast-food company, did not decline throughout the downturn. Panera Bread, an American fast-food chain known for its fresh ingredients, performed well, too, because it offers higher-quality food at lower prices than restaurants.
paragraphs.translationZh: C）因此，快餐连锁店比价格更高的竞争对手更好地经受住了经济衰退。 2009年，美国全方位服务餐厅的销售额下降了6%以上，但快餐连锁店的总销售额基本保持不变。在日本、法国和英国等一些市场，快餐总支出有所增加。全球最大的快餐公司麦当劳在美国的同店销售额在整个经济低迷时期并未下降。以新鲜食材闻名的美国快餐连锁店 Panera Bread 也表现出色，因为它以比餐馆更低的价格提供更高品质的食品。

paragraphs.sourceText: D) But not all fast-food companies have been as fortunate. Many, such as Burger King, have seen sales fall. In a severe recession, while some people trade down to fast food, many others eat at home more frequently to save money. David Palmer，an analyst at UBS，a bank，says smaller fast- food chains in America，such as Jack in the Box and Carl’s Jr.， have been hit particularly hard in this downturn because they are competing with the global giant McDonald^, which increased spending on advertising by more than 7% last year as others cut back.
paragraphs.translationZh: D) 但并非所有快餐公司都这么幸运。汉堡王等许多公司的销售额都出现了下降。在严重的经济衰退中，虽然有些人转而吃快餐，但许多人为了省钱而更频繁地在家吃饭。瑞银集团(UBS)分析师大卫·帕尔默(David Palmer)表示，美国规模较小的快餐连锁店，例如Jack in the Box和Carl's Jr.，在这次经济低迷中受到的打击尤其严重，因为它们正在与全球巨头麦当劳竞争，而麦当劳去年在广告支出上增加了7%以上，而其他公司却在削减广告支出。

paragraphs.sourceText: E) Some fast-food companies also sacrificed their own profits by trying to give customers better value.During the recession companies set prices low, hoping that once they had tempted customers through the door they would be persuaded to order more expensive items. But in many cases that strategy did not work. Last year Burger franchisees(特许经营人)sued（起诉） the company over its double-cheeseburger promotion, claiming it was unfair for them to be repuired to sell these for $1 when they cost $1.10 to make. In May a judge ruled in favour of Burger King. Nevertheless, the company may still be cursing its decision to promote cheap choices over more expensive ones because items on its “value menu” now account for around 20% of all sales, up from 12% last October.
paragraphs.translationZh: E) 一些快餐公司还牺牲了自己的利润，试图为顾客提供更好的价值。在经济衰退期间，公司将价格定得很低，希望一旦吸引顾客进门，他们就会被说服订购更昂贵的商品。但在很多情况下，这一策略并没有奏效。去年，汉堡特许经营人就双层芝士汉堡的促销活动起诉该公司，声称他们被要求以 1 美元的价格出售这些汉堡，而这些汉堡的制作成本为 1.10 美元，这对他们来说是不公平的。五月，法官作出了对汉堡王有利的裁决。尽管如此，该公司可能仍在抱怨其推广廉价商品而不是昂贵商品的决定，因为其“超值菜单”上的商品目前约占总销售额的 20%，高于去年 10 月的 12%。

paragraphs.sourceText: F) Analysts expect the fast-food industry to grow modestly this year. But the downturn is making companies rethink their strategies. Many are now introducing higher-priced items to entice (引诱）consumers away from $1 specials. RFC, a division of Yum! Brands，which also owns Taco Bell and Pizza Hut, has launched a chicken sandwich that costs around $5. And in May Burger King introduced barbecue(烧烤）pork ribs at $7 for eight.
paragraphs.translationZh: F) 分析师预计今年快餐行业将温和增长。但经济低迷正在促使企业重新考虑其战略。许多公司现在推出了更高价的产品来吸引消费者远离 1 美元的特价商品。 RFC 是 Yum! Brands 的一个部门，它还拥有 Taco Bell 和必胜客，推出了价格约为 5 美元的鸡肉三明治。5 月，汉堡王推出了烧烤排骨，价格为 7 美元/8 块。

paragraphs.sourceText: G) Companies are also trying to get customers to buy new and more items, including drinks. McDonald’s started selling better coffee as a challenge to Starbucks. Its “ McCafe ’’ line now accounts for an estimated 6% of sales in America. Starbucks has sold rights to its Seattle’s Best coffee brand to Burger King, which will start selling it later this year.
paragraphs.translationZh: G) 公司还试图让顾客购买新的和更多的商品，包括饮料。麦当劳开始销售更好的咖啡，作为对星巴克的挑战。其“McCafe”系列目前估计占美国销售额的 6%。星巴克已将其西雅图最佳咖啡品牌的权利出售给汉堡王，汉堡王将于今年晚些时候开始出售该品牌。

paragraphs.sourceText: H) As fast-food companies shift from “super size” to “more buys”，they need to keep customer traffic high throughout the day. Many see breakfast as a big opportunity, and not just for fatty food. McDonald’s will start selling porridge (粥）in America next year. Breakfast has the potential to be very profitable, says Sara Senatore of Bernstein, a research firm, because the margins can be high. Fast-food companies are also adding midday and late-night snacks, such as blended drinks and wraps. The idea is that by having a greater range of things on the menu, “we can sell to consumers products they want all day,” says Rick Carucci, the chief financial officer of Yum! Brands.
paragraphs.translationZh: H) 随着快餐公司从“超大规模”转向“更多购买”，他们需要保持全天的高客流量。许多人认为早餐是一个巨大的机会，而不仅仅是脂肪食物。麦当劳明年将开始在美国销售粥。研究公司 Bernstein 的 Sara Senatore 表示，早餐有可能非常有利可图，因为利润可能很高。快餐公司也在增加午间和深夜小吃，例如混合饮料和卷饼。我们的想法是，通过在菜单上提供更多种类的东西，“我们可以向消费者出售他们全天想要的产品，”百胜餐饮集团首席财务官 Rick Carucci 说！品牌。

paragraphs.sourceText: I) But what about those growing waistlines? So far, fast-food firms have cleverly avoided government regulation. By providing healthy options, like salads and low-calorie sandwiches, they have at least given the impression of doing something about helping to fight obesity (肥胖症）.These offerings are not necessarily loss-leaders, as they broaden the appeal of outlets to groups of diners that include some people who don’t want to eat a burger. But customers cannot be forced to order salads instead of fries.
paragraphs.translationZh: I) 但是那些不断增长的腰围呢？到目前为止，快餐公司巧妙地避开了政府监管。通过提供健康的选择，如沙拉和低热量三明治，他们至少给人留下了在帮助对抗肥胖方面采取措施的印象。这些产品不一定是亏本的，因为它们扩大了餐厅对食客群体的吸引力，其中包括一些不想吃汉堡的人。但不能强迫顾客点沙拉而不是薯条。

paragraphs.sourceText: J) In the future, simply offering a healthy option may not be good enough. “Every packaged-food and restaurant company I know is concerned about regulation right now,” says Mr. Palmer of UBS. America’s health-reform bill, which Congress passed this year, requires restaurant chains with 20 or more outlets to put the calorie-content of items they serve on the menu. A study by the National Bureau of Economic Research, which tracked the effects on Starbucks of a similar calorie-posting law in New York City in 2007, found that the average calorie-count per transaction fell 6% and revenue increased 3% at Starbucks stores where a Dunkin Donuts outlet was nearby—a sign, it is said, that menu-labelling could favour chains that have more healthy offerings.
paragraphs.translationZh: J) 将来，仅仅提供健康的选择可能还不够。 “我所知道的每家包装食品和餐饮公司现在都担心监管问题，”瑞银的帕尔默先生说。国会今年通过的美国医疗改革法案要求拥有 20 家或以上门店的连锁餐厅将其提供的菜肴的卡路里含量列入菜单。美国国家经济研究局的一项研究跟踪了 2007 年纽约市类似卡路里公布法对星巴克的影响，发现在附近有 Dunkin Donuts 门店的星巴克门店，每笔交易的平均卡路里计数下降了 6%，收入增加了 3%——据说，这表明菜单标签可能有利于提供更健康产品的连锁店。

paragraphs.sourceText: K) In order to avoid other legislation in America and elsewhere, fast-food companies will have to continue innovating (创新). Walt Riker of McDonald’s claims the change it has made in its menu means it offers more healthy items than it did a few years ago. “We probably sell more vegetables, more milk, more salads, more apples than any restaurant business in the world," he says. But the recent proposal by a county in California to ban McDonald’s from including toys in its high-calorie "Happy Meals”, because legislators believe it attracts children to unhealthy food, suggests there is a lot more left to do.
paragraphs.translationZh: K) 为了避免美国和其他地方的其他立法，快餐公司将不得不继续创新。麦当劳的沃尔特·赖克(Walt Riker)声称，菜单上所做的改变意味着它提供了比几年前更多的健康食品。 “我们销售的蔬菜、牛奶、沙拉、苹果可能比世界上任何一家餐馆都多，”他说。但加利福尼亚州一个县最近提议禁止麦当劳在其高热量“开心乐园餐”中添加玩具，因为立法者认为这会吸引儿童吃不健康的食物，这表明还有很多事情要做。

paragraphs.sourceText: 46. Some people propose laws be made to stop McDonald’s from attaching toys to its food specials for children.
paragraphs.translationZh: 46. 一些人提议制定法律，阻止麦当劳在其儿童特价食品中添加玩具。

paragraphs.sourceText: 47. Fast-food firms may not be able to cope with pressures from food regulation in the near future.
paragraphs.translationZh: 47. 快餐公司在不久的将来可能无法应对食品监管的压力。

paragraphs.sourceText: 48. Burger King will start to sell Seattle’s Best coffee to increase sales.
paragraphs.translationZh: 48. 汉堡王将开始销售西雅图最好的咖啡以增加销量。

paragraphs.sourceText: Questions 56 to 60 are based on the following passage.
paragraphs.translationZh: 第 56 至 60 题基于以下段落。

paragraphs.sourceText: If you think a high-factor sunscreen (防晒霜) keeps you safe from harmful rays, you may be wrong. Research in this week^ Nature shows that while factor 50 reduces the number of melanomas (黑瘤）and delays their occurrence, it can’t prevent them. Melanomas are the most aggressive skin cancers. You have a higher risk if you have red or blond hair, fair skin, blue or green eyes, or sunburn easily, or if a close relative has had one. Melanomas are more common if you have periodic intense exposure to the sun. Other skin cancers are increasingly likely with long-term exposure.
paragraphs.translationZh: 如果您认为高因子防晒霜可以让您免受有害射线的侵害，那么您可能错了。本周^《自然》杂志的研究表明，虽然因子 50 可以减少黑色素瘤（黑瘤）的数量并延缓其发生，但它无法预防它们。黑色素瘤是最具侵袭性的皮肤癌。如果您有红色或金色头发、白皙皮肤、蓝色或绿色眼睛、容易晒伤，或者近亲曾患有黑色素瘤，那么您的风险会更高。如果您定期强烈暴露在阳光下，则黑色素瘤会更常见。长期暴露在阳光下，其他皮肤癌的可能性会增加。

paragraphs.sourceText: There is continuing debate as to how effective sunscreen is in reducing melanomas—the evidence is weaker than it is for preventing other types of skin cancer. A 2011 Australian study of 1,621 people found that people randomly selected to apply sunscreen daily had half the rate of melanomas of people who used cream as needed. A second study, comparing 1,167 people with melanomas to 1,101 who didn’t have the cancer, found that using sunscreen routinely, alongside other protection such as hats, long sleeves or staying in the shade, did give some protection. This study said other forms of sun protection—not sunscreen—seemed most beneficial. The study relied on people remembering what they had done over each decade of their lives, so it’s not entirely reliable. But it seems reasonable to think sunscreen gives people a false sense of security in the sun.
paragraphs.translationZh: 关于防晒霜在减少黑色素瘤方面的效果如何，一直存在争论——与预防其他类型皮肤癌相比，其证据较弱。 2011 年澳大利亚对 1,621 人进行的一项研究发现，随机选择每天涂抹防晒霜的人患黑色素瘤的几率是按需使用防晒霜的人的一半。第二项研究对 1,167 名患有黑色素瘤的人与 1,101 名未患黑色素瘤的人进行了比较，结果发现，定期使用防晒霜，再加上帽子、长袖衣服或呆在阴凉处等其他保护措施，确实能起到一定的保护作用。这项研究称，其他形式的防晒——而不是防晒霜——似乎最有益。这项研究依赖于人们记住他们一生中每十年所做的事情，因此它并不完全可靠。但认为防晒霜给人们在阳光下带来错误的安全感的想法似乎是合理的。

paragraphs.sourceText: Many people also don’t use sunscreen properly—applying insufficient amounts, failing to reapply after a couple of hours and staying in the sun too long. It is sunburn that is most worrying—recent research shows five episodes of sunburn in the teenage years increases the risk of all skin cancers.
paragraphs.translationZh: 许多人也没有正确使用防晒霜——涂抹量不足，几个小时后没有重新涂抹，以及在阳光下停留的时间太长。最令人担忧的是晒伤——最近的研究表明，青少年时期五次晒伤会增加患所有皮肤癌的风险。

paragraphs.sourceText: The good news is that a combination of sunscreen and covering up can reduce melanoma rates, as shown by Australian figures from their slip-slop-slap campaign. So if there is a heat wave this summer, it would be best for us, too, to slip on a shirt, slop on(补上) sunscreen and slap on a hat.
paragraphs.translationZh: 好消息是，防晒霜和遮盖物的结合可以降低黑色素瘤的发病率，正如澳大利亚的 slip-slop-slap 活动的数据所显示的那样。所以，如果今年夏天有热浪，我们最好也穿上衬衫，补上防晒霜，戴上帽子。

paragraphs.sourceText: Questions 61 to 65 are based on the following passage.
paragraphs.translationZh: 第 61 至 65 题基于以下段落。

paragraphs.sourceText: Across the rich world, well-educated people increasingly work longer than the less-skilled. Some 65% of American men aged 62 - 74 with a professional degree are in the workforce, compared with 32% of men with only a high-school certificate. This gap is part of a deepening divide between the well-educated well-off and the unskilled poor. Rapid technological advance has raised the incomes of the highly skilled while squeezing those of the unskilled. The consequences, for individuals and society, are profound.
paragraphs.translationZh: 在富裕国家，受过良好教育的人比技能较低的人工作时间越来越长。 62-74 岁的美国男性中，大约 65% 拥有专业学位，而只有高中文凭的男性中这一比例为 32%。这种差距是受过良好教育的富人和无技能的穷人之间日益加深的鸿沟的一部分。快速的技术进步提高了高技能人群的收入，同时挤压了低技能人群的收入。对于个人和社会来说，其后果是深远的。

paragraphs.sourceText: The world is facing an astonishing rise in the number of old people, and they will live longer than ever before. Over the next 20 years the global population of those aged 65 or more will almost double, from 600 million to 1. 1 billion. The experience of the 20th century, when greater longevity(长寿）translated into more years in retirement rather than more years at work, has persuaded many observers that this shift will lead to slower economic growth, while the swelling ranks of pensioners will create government budget problems.
paragraphs.translationZh: 世界正面临老年人数量惊人增长的问题，而且他们的寿命将比以往任何时候都要长。未来 20 年，全球 65 岁或以上的人口将几乎翻倍，从 6 亿增至 11 亿。 20世纪的经验表明，长寿意味着退休时间更长，而不是工作时间更长，这让许多观察家相信，这种转变将导致经济增长放缓，而养老金领取者队伍的膨胀将造成政府预算问题。

paragraphs.sourceText: But the notion of a sharp division between the working young and the idle old misses a new trend, the growing gap between the skilled and the unskilled. Employment rates are falling among younger unskilled people, whereas older skilled folk are working longer. The divide is most extreme in America, where well-educated baby-boomers (二战后生育高峰期出生的美国人）are putting off retirement while many less-skilled younger people have dropped out of the workforce.
paragraphs.translationZh: 但是，工作的年轻人和游手好闲的老年人之间存在明显区别的观念忽视了一个新趋势，即熟练工人和非熟练工人之间日益扩大的差距。年轻的非技术人员的就业率正在下降，而年长的技术人员的工作时间则更长。这种差距在美国最为严重，受过良好教育的婴儿潮一代出生的美国人正在推迟退休，而许多技能较差的年轻人则退出了劳动力市场。

paragraphs.sourceText: Policy is partly responsible. Many European governments have abandoned policies that used to encourage people to retire early. Rising life expectancy(预期寿命), combined with the replacement of generous defined-benefit pension plans with less generous defined-contribution ones, means that even the better-off must work longer to have a comfortable retirement. But the changing nature of work also plays a big role. Pay has risen sharply for the highly educated, and those people continue to reap rich rewards into old age because these days the educated elderly are more productive than the preceding generation. Technological change may well reinforce that shift: the skills that complement computers, from management knowhow to creativity, do not necessarily decline with age.
paragraphs.translationZh: 政策负有部分责任。许多欧洲政府已经放弃了过去鼓励人们提前退休的政策。预期寿命的延长，加上慷慨的固定福利养老金计划被不太慷慨的固定缴款计划所取代，意味着即使是较富裕的人也必须工作更长的时间才能过上舒适的退休生活。但工作性质的变化也发挥着重要作用。受过高等教育的人的工资大幅上涨，这些人到了晚年仍能获得丰厚的回报，因为如今受过教育的老年人比上一代人更有生产力。技术变革很可能会强化这种转变：与计算机相辅相成的技能，从管理知识到创造力，并不一定会随着年龄的增长而下降。
